purpose: WI-397 perf/budget regression baselines. Ceilings/counts are the CONTRACT, set at/above current measured values to catch RE-bloat — the scar-tissue accumulation WI-369 only measures, made fail-closed here. A real justified increase means re-measuring and bumping this file in the same change (a deliberate, reviewed act).

context_budget.always_on_rules_note: The always-on rule SET is derived dynamically by the validator from skills-manifest.json rulesRegistry entries with auto_inject:"always" (currently 6) — NOT a hardcoded list here, so a new always-on rule is automatically counted (Gemini G6 #2).

hook_spawn.note: Spawn COUNT per lifecycle event (deterministic; warm wall-clock is environment-flaky so we gate count, the real latency driver — each hook is a process spawn per matching tool event). Adding a hook fails this until the count is bumped here deliberately, forcing a latency-review. WI-384: PreToolUse 10→11 for svc-learning-inject (action-time learning injection). WI-392: PreToolUse 11→12 for svc-owner-inject (action-time intended-owner routing; fail-open + small lib + memo-cached; high value — attacks the #1 measured wrong-approach friction). WI-399 A1: PreToolUse 12->11 (svc-phase-boundary-detector merged into svc-workflow-guard default mode — same checks, one spawn) and svc-preflight-skill matcher narrowed *->Skill (runtime no-op spawns eliminated on every non-Skill tool event; count unchanged, latency win is per-event). WI-CLN-13 (plan §4.15): SubagentStart/SubagentStop each 0→1 for the new subagent telemetry hooks — these fire only on subagent lifecycle (spawn/stop), NOT per tool call, so they add no hot-path latency; both are append-only fail-open observers.

hook_latency_informational.note: WI-399 B7 measured baseline (informational ONLY — wall-clock is environment-flaky, the tier-1 gate stays on COUNT per WI-397 design). Measured 2026-06-10 on WSL2, node cold-start ~40-50ms, best-of-3 per hook.
